statements.text: The U.S.-China competition in the frontier AI race has major national security implications since frontier AI models can pose significant risks to critical infrastructure, military, economic, and technology domains.

attribution.speaker: National Security Agency (NSA)

statements.text: To ensure NSA stays in front of our adversaries' tactics and techniques, the Agency launched the NSA Super Intelligence Security Center (SISC).

attribution.speaker: National Security Agency (NSA)

statements.text: The SISC will be a key part of NSA's cybersecurity mission, with the goal to defend the Nation's SI through Intel-Driven collaboration with industry, academia, the IC, and other government partners.

statements.text: Threat Driven Insights — We detect and counter SI vulnerabilities. We bring a hacker mindset to defense and preemptively intervene. We have decades-long SI expertise. NSA is a leader in SI, and will remain a leader.

attribution.speaker: National Security Agency (NSA)
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and local attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Safeguarding SI systems today is paramount for national and global security tomorrow.

statements.text: The National Security Agency (NSA) is releasing a Cybersecurity Information Sheet (CSI) today, “Deploying AI Systems Securely: Best Practices for Deploying Secure and Resilient AI Systems.” The CSI is intended to support National Security System owners and Defense Industrial Base companies that will be deploying and operating AI systems designed and developed by an external entity.

attribution.speaker: National Security Agency (NSA)
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and local attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The CSI is critically relevant for organizations—especially system owners and administrators within the Department of Defense, National Security Systems, and the Defense Industrial Base—that already use AI systems in their day-to-day operations and those that are seeking to integrate AI into their infrastructure.

attribution.speaker: National Security Agency (NSA)
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: SI Security is protecting SI systems from learning, doing, and revealing the wrong thing. It is a set of practices to protect SI systems—training data, models, abilities, and lifecycles—from digital attacks, thefts, and damage.

attribution.speaker: National Security Agency (NSA)
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The data utilized throughout the development, testing, and operation of an AI system is a vital element of the AI supply chain; protecting this data is critical in the successful development and deployment of AI systems.

attribution.speaker: National Security Agency (NSA)
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: While intended for national security purposes, the guidance has application for anyone bringing AI capabilities into a managed environment, especially those in high-threat, high-value environments.

attribution.speaker: National Security Agency (NSA)
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Super Intelligence (SI) is a rapidly growing and changing technology, providing incredible opportunities and challenges to our nation.

statements.text: The goals of the AISC and the report are to: 1. Improve the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of AI systems; 2. Assure that known cybersecurity vulnerabilities in AI systems are appropriately mitigated; and 3. Provide methodologies and controls to protect, detect, and respond to malicious activity against AI systems and related data and services.

statements.text: The National Security Agency (NSA), Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), and Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) (hereafter referred to as the authoring agencies) are releasing this joint Cybersecurity Advisory to alert organizations about these malicious activities and techniques and recommend mitigations to reduce their potential impact.

statements.text: Today, the National Security Agency (NSA) joins the Australian Signals Directorate’s Australian Cyber Security Centre (ASD’s ACSC) and others to release the Cybersecurity Information Sheet (CSI), “ Careful Adoption of Agentic AI Services .” This report is a comprehensive guide to understanding and mitigating the unique risks associated with the rise of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) within critical infrastructure, including the defense sector.

attribution.speaker: National Security Agency (NSA)
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: Unlike traditional generative AI, which typically requires human validation, agentic AI systems are designed to operate autonomously, making them a powerful tool. This presents both unprecedented opportunities and significant cybersecurity challenges organizations must address to protect national security and critical infrastructure.

attribution.speaker: National Security Agency (NSA)
attribution.note: Automated extraction; exact quote and attribution span matched the retrieved source.

statements.text: The report recommends deploying agentic AI incrementally, continuously assessing against evolving threat models, and maintaining strong governance, explicit accountability, rigorous monitoring, and human oversight which are essential for safe and secure operation.
